Summary:
Aurora Biotech requested a focused security/compliance review covering prompt/content retention options, explicit confirmation of 'no training on customer data', KMS/customer-managed key patterns, encryption at rest/in-transit, audit logging, RBAC/SSO setup, and data residency to ensure EU-only processing for a regulated dataset. Redwood AE + SE walked through architecture, controls, and practical next steps including a staging test against customer-managed KMS in eu-west-1 and contract language follow-up.

Topics covered:
- No-training-on-customer-data pledge and contractual wording
- Prompt retention TTL and ephemeral modes
- KMS: customer-managed keys, HSM / Cloud KMS integration, key rotation
- SSO/SAML with Okta, RBAC, SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs: granularity, retention, access
- Data residency: region pinning and fallback controls
- Handling of PII/PHI and segregation in Dedicated/Private modes

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Maya, Anika, Rafael, Ellen — hi. Quick agenda: run through the security architecture, address the "no training" ask, KMS options, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:00:22] Maya Chen (Aurora): Yes, thanks Lucas. We're on a tight compliance window so we wanna be explicit about data residency and any possibility our prompts could be used for model training.
[00:00:38] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Totally understood. We'll go through the short and long answers. Short answer: we have a contractual no-train commitment for hosted accounts and by default data is not used to train Redwood models. Longer: there's a control plane/data plane separation, and for extra assurance we support Dedicated/Private where you control keys and network.
[00:01:05] Anika Patel (Head of Security): When you say "contractual no-train" is that in standard T&Cs or do we need a separate clause? Ellen, are we expecting redlines?
[00:01:20] Ellen Park (Legal): We'll likely request explicit language in the Master Services Agreement and the DPA that says 'no model training' and clarify retention windows. Also need audit log access and SOC2 artifacts.
[00:01:40] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Absolutely. We can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs — I'll share the links after the call. We can put explicit no-train wording in the DPA; many enterprise customers get that.
[00:01:55] Rafael Gomez (ML Eng): Two technical Qs up front: if we use hosted API but request no retention, is there any in-flight caching or KV cache that could persist input tokens beyond request lifetime?
[00:02:12] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Great question. There are two layers: runtime KV cache for latency/auto-batching which is ephemeral per session and not persisted to disk; and then the default backend request logs which are configurable. If you want zero retention, we can enable ephemeral prompts where request logs are not stored beyond X minutes and no prompts are included in analytics. For absolute control we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS.
[00:02:40] [00:02:40] Speaker 1: (murmur) mm-hmm
[00:02:52] Anika Patel (Aurora): For regulatory reasons we need data residency in EU only. How does region pinning work? What happens on degradation / fallback?
[00:03:06] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We support region pinning at the deployment level. You can pin to eu-west-1, and the control plane will route inference to that region. There are fallback policies but for regulated accounts we can disable cross-region fallback — it becomes a hard constraint. In Dedicated/Private we can also keep control plane in VPC.
[00:03:32] Maya Chen (Aurora): Ok, can you guarantee that logs won't be copied to other regions for analytics?
[00:03:40] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We can sign that in the DPA: logs for pinned deployments are stored in the pinned region only. For hosted non-pinned routes we keep logs in nearest region for performance unless customer requests different.
[00:03:53] [00:03:53] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Also note that in the console you can set the log retention TTL per project — default is 30 days for analytics but you can shorten to 0 for ephemeral projects.
[00:04:12] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): About KMS — can we bring our own CMK from our Azure Key Vault or Google Cloud KMS? We need HSM-backed keys.
[00:04:25] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We support cloud-provider KMS integrations. For hosted we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault through an integration pattern; HSM-backed keys are supported if the cloud KMS offers them. For Dedicated/Private you can either use our service to reference your external KMS or run the KMS inside your VPC and we call it via private connectivity.
[00:04:46] Anika Patel (Aurora): Does Redwood ever hold the plaintext keys?
[00:04:51] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): No, in the BYOK pattern we store only references and encrypted blobs; keys remain in the provider's KMS. For customer-managed CMKs we never exfiltrate the raw key material.
[00:05:10] [00:05:10] Lucas Hart (Redwood): To be clear: encryption at rest is AES256; in-transit is TLS1.3. For additional controls we support envelope encryption with CMK and per-tenant key separation.
[00:05:25] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): Audit log access — what level of detail can we get? We need ability to show who accessed what prompt, by which API key, and operator actions in the console.
[00:05:38] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We capture admin events, API calls, model invocations, and policy changes with timestamps and caller identity. You can stream logs to your SIEM via our Log Exporter (supports syslog/CloudWatch/GCP Logging) and we can provide an audit-friendly export in NDJSON. Retention windows can be configured.
[00:05:58] Maya Chen (Aurora): Is there a way to mask PII automatically before it reaches the model? We have PHI in many prompts.
[00:06:08] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We provide optional pre-processing hooks — customers can run a redact step via Lambda/webhook or use our built-in redaction pipeline to detect and redact common PII/PHI patterns. Redaction runs before tokens are sent to model. Note: redaction is heuristic so we recommend combining with deterministic tokenization for high-risk workflows.
[00:06:30] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): If redaction fails, is there any quarantine or alerting?
[00:06:34] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): You can enable a rule to block requests that match high-risk patterns and send them to a quarantine queue. We also support DLP integrations for more advanced checks.
[00:06:47] [00:06:47] Speaker 2: (typing)
[00:06:55] Anika Patel (Aurora): About the 'no training' claim — how do you operationalize it? Is it just an agreement or is there a tech control?
[00:07:05] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Both. For hosted accounts we have a default policy that excludes customer prompt/response data from model training pipelines. We have legal commitments (DPA) and technical separation: data used for training is ingested from a different internal pipeline and requires explicit opt-in and transformations. For extra assurance, Dedicated/Private offers full data isolation so no central training ingestion occurs.
[00:07:30] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): We will want explicit auditability that training pipelines don't include customer datasets — some clients have asked for attestation statements.
[00:07:39] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We can provide an attestation/statement of practices and include it as an addendum. We also recently added an internal quarterly audit that checks training pipelines and we can share a redacted summary.
[00:07:56] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): If we do a POC on hosted with ephemeral retention, what's our evidence that nothing persisted? Could we run a red-team to check?
[00:08:05] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Yes — common approach: run a blackbox test and then request an export of logs, retention TTL settings, and a signed statement from our security team for the test window. For staging we can also run the POC in a pinned EU deployment with CMK and ephemeral TTL and provide logs showing no persisted prompt bodies.
[00:08:26] [00:08:26] Maya Chen (Aurora): Ok. On contract language about 'no training' we also want a clause on derivative data — outputs or embeddings used in service improvements.
[00:08:36] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We can be explicit: no customer data or derivatives will be used to improve models unless you opt-in. Derivatives used for telemetry/metrics are aggregate and non-identifying; we'll scope that in the DPA.
[00:08:50] Anika Patel (Aurora): How about RBAC — can we map our internal roles to Redwood roles via SCIM? We need fine-grained admin separation.
[00:08:59] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): SCIM provisioning is supported. We have built-in roles (Admin, Developer, Auditor, ReadOnly) and you can map SAML groups to these roles during provisioning. We also support session timeouts, MFA enforced at IdP, and session revocation.
[00:09:18] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): For legal compliance, we'd like immutable audit logs for certain admin actions for six years. Is that realistic?
[00:09:28] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We usually recommend streaming logs to your SIEM for long-term retention. We can negotiate retention add-ons for Redwood-managed storage, but standard platform retention is shorter. We'll include options and costs in the follow-up.
[00:09:45] [00:09:45] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): A small nit: when you say ephemeral TTL for prompts, what unit is it — seconds? minutes? We need definitive numbers to show auditors.
[00:09:55] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Ephemeral TTL is configurable; typical settings are 0 (no persistence), 15 minutes, 24 hours. For auditors, we can provide the configuration manifest showing TTL=0 during the POC and the export proving no records were created.
[00:10:15] Maya Chen (Aurora): If we go Dedicated, do we need to bring any infra? What are lead times?
[00:10:22] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Dedicated can be on Redwood-managed infra or co-located. Lead times vary based on GPU capacity and region — typically 6-8 weeks for standard profiles; faster if you're flexible on hardware. For regulated workloads many customers start with a hosted-pinned deployment for the short term then move to Dedicated for long-term.
[00:10:40] Anika Patel (Aurora): For compliance evidence, can we get a runbook of who did what during a retention change?
[00:10:47] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Yes, our console records admin changes with who/when/what and we can export that as part of the audit package.
[00:10:58] [00:10:58] Speaker 3: (background)
[00:11:06] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): We're also worried about subcontractors — does Redwood share any data with third parties?
[00:11:12] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We disclose subprocessors in the DPA and keep an up-to-date list. For customers requiring tighter control we can restrict which subprocessors are used or run Private deployments with no external subprocessors.
[00:11:27] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Two more tech checks: tokenization; do you store raw text anywhere for embedding indexes? We plan to store embeddings but not the plaintext.
[00:11:37] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): You can choose what we store. We support storing embeddings only (vector store) with a pointer to your ID, and we can prevent storing the raw prompt by setting the store_prompt flag to false. That prevents plaintext from being written to the index.
[00:11:53] Maya Chen (Aurora): Great. Related: multi-tenancy — how do you ensure tenant isolation in Dedicated?
[00:11:59] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Dedicated is physically isolated pools and per-tenant containers/processes. We also support per-tenant keys and VPC peering for network isolation.
[00:12:10] [00:12:10] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Quick demo note: we'll share a small step-by-step for the staging test so Rafael can spin it up.
[00:12:16] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Perfect. Could Priya drop the SAML metadata and an example assertion?
[00:12:21] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Yes, I'll include a sample assertion and SAML metadata in the follow-up.
[00:12:28] [00:12:28] Ellen Park (Aurora): From contracting side we want to add an escrow clause for logs and keys in certain events. Is that supported?
[00:12:37] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We can discuss escrow options — often customers request a mechanism where logs are escrowed with a third party under clear triggers. We'll involve Legal on that.
[00:12:48] Maya Chen (Aurora): Anything on continuous monitoring / detection? We need security posture reports.
[00:12:54] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We produce monthly security posture summaries for enterprise customers and can enable continuous monitoring exports for SIEM.
[00:13:10] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Let's talk about a realistic test plan for the POC — I'd like to confirm we can run it without any data leaving eu-west-1 and with CMK.
[00:13:19] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Proposed POC: 1) Create staging project pinned to eu-west-1 with TTL=0, store_prompt=false; 2) Configure BYOK CMK (customer-managed) and run a small set of representative prompts; 3) Request logs and signed attestation for the test window. Rafael to provision staging and run tests, Redwood provides artifacts.
[00:13:42] Anika Patel (Aurora): Timeline? We need this done before our audit window in early April.
[00:13:48] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We can prioritize — send artifacts by 3/22, run the POC week of 3/23, deliver attestation by 3/30.
[00:13:57] [00:13:57] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): I'll add a templated runbook to the follow-up so you can reproduce it.
[00:14:05] Maya Chen (Aurora): Good. One more question: embeddings — are they considered training data if stored?
[00:14:12] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): By default, embeddings stored in your account are not used for model training. We'll add explicit contract language that embeddings and derivatives aren't used for training without opt-in.
[00:14:25] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): We'll want the opt-in process described — legal signoff + technical flags.
[00:14:32] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Noted. We'll include that in the DPA addendum.
[00:14:40] [00:14:40] Speaker 4: (crosstalk)
[00:14:52] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): A nit on metrics: can we ingest telemetry but only as counters and histograms, never as raw tokens?
[00:15:00] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Yes, that's our recommended telemetry model for regulated customers — aggregate metrics only.
[00:15:10] Maya Chen (Aurora): If we go with ephemeral TTL=0, will debug logs still contain request bodies?
[00:15:18] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Debug logs are separate and can be disabled for ephemeral projects. We can also redact request bodies in debug logs.
[00:15:30] [00:15:30] Lucas Hart (Redwood): I'll share a redacted example audit export in the follow-up so you can see the fields we capture.
[00:15:38] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): Regarding the subprocessors list — can you provide a signed copy?
[00:15:45] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We'll provide the latest subprocessors LOE and we can include it in the DPA package.
[00:15:57] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Any constraints on peak TPS for Dedicated in eu-west-1?
[00:16:03] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Depends on instance type and batch config; we'll propose profiles — example: 200 req/s sustained for the XG profile. We'll include detailed perf numbers in the follow-up.

[00:16:28] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We'll provide SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 certificate, recent pentest summary (redacted), and the attestation on training pipelines. SOC2 link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (will share private link).
[00:16:40] Anika Patel (Aurora): For pentest, we need the dates and the vendor name.
[00:16:44] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We'll include vendor and date in the summary we share.
[00:16:52] [00:16:52] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Quick architecture note for the runbook: the staging flow will show TLS enforced, CMK used for envelope encryption, and logs streamed to your SIEM with TTL=0.
[00:17:03] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Perfect. If we see any artifacts in indexes during the POC, what's the remediation SLA?
[00:17:11] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We have an incident response SLA for remediation — we'll commit to a priority timeline in the contract addendum for high-severity data exposure incidents.
[00:17:22] Maya Chen (Aurora): Can Redwood support a legal hold on logs if needed?
[00:17:28] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): This is important — in case of a subpoena we may need preservation.
[00:17:33] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): We can enable legal-hold flags for specific projects and export snapshots to your custody. That would be an operational runbook we'll add to the follow-up.
[00:17:46] [00:17:46] Speaker 5: (chair creak)
[00:17:57] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): Are server-side caches ever persisted to disk for long contexts?
[00:18:02] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): No, persistent disk is not used for session KV cache. For very long contexts we page to ephemeral memory and it's cleared after the session.
[00:18:16] Maya Chen (Aurora): We also want to know who in Redwood can sign the attestation.
[00:18:22] Lucas Hart (Redwood): Typically Security or the VP of Engineering signs attestations. We'll coordinate and include a signatory name in the attestation.
[00:18:33] [00:18:33] Ellen Park (Aurora Legal): Ok. On the follow-up I'd like explicit DPA language examples for: no training; embeddings not used; regional log residency; key-control.
[00:18:45] Lucas Hart (Redwood): We'll prepare DPA redline suggestions to accelerate review.
[00:18:53] Rafael Gomez (Aurora): One last technical — model fallbacks. If pinned eu-west-1 model is capacity-starved, do you ever route to other models in other regions?
[00:19:03] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Not if you disable fallback. For enterprise-grade pinned deployments we disable cross-region fallback by policy. We can also configure fallback to a lower-capacity model in the same region only.
[00:19:17] Maya Chen (Aurora): Good. Anything else from Redwood?
